title: Posterior Contraction Rates for sparse Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Anisotropic Besov Spaces
claim: The architecture is built hierarchically: a network of learnable edge functions, each a sparse combination of a fixed basis, as in a zoom-in decomposition.
layout: 3 panels: large left network, two stacked right zoom-ins, curved arrows
description: A three-panel figure. The left panel, '1. KAN', shows a layered network with inputs x1..xd at the bottom and output f_theta(x) at the top. A bracket marks the max width D. Black edges connect nodes, and small thumbnail boxes with spline curves sit on the edges, labelled Φ0, Φ1 and Φ_{L-1}. Dotted lines stand in for omitted layers. One edge at the top is circled in orange, and a gray arrow leads from it to the upper-right panel, '2. Sparse edge function'. That panel gives the formula for φ as a SiLU term plus a spline sum. Below the formula is a coefficient-sparsity strip with bars between the bounds ±B, and a plot of an orange curve over a green SiLU curve and blue basis bumps. A second arrow leads to the lower-right panel, '3. B-spline basis', which shows overlapping gray bumps on a knot axis from -H to H, with formulas. Orange highlights tie the panels together.
caption: Sparse fixed-knot B-spline KAN construction. The left panel shows a KAN with layer widths bounded by D; edges carry learnable univariate functions. The upper-right panel zooms in on one edge function with coefficient-level sparsity, the uniform coefficient bound B, and a SiLU component. The lower-right panel zooms further into the B-spline basis used in the spline part of the edge function.
abstract: We study posterior contraction rates for sparse Bayesian Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) over anisotropic Besov spaces, providing a statistical foundation for KANs from a Bayesian point of view. We show that sparse Bayesian KANs equipped with spike-and-slab-type sparsity priors attain a near-minimax posterior contraction rate. In particular, the contraction rate depends on the intrinsic anisotropic smoothness of the underlying function. Moreover, by placing a hyperprior on a single model-size parameter, the resulting posterior adapts to unknown anisotropic smoothness and still achieves the corresponding near-minimax rate. A distinctive feature of our results, compared with those for standard multilayer perceptrons, is that the KAN depth can be kept fixed: owing to the expressive power of learnable spline edge functions, the required approximation complexity is controlled through the network width, the range and size of the spline grid, and parameter sparsity. Our analysis develops theoretical tools tailored to sparse spline-edge architectures, including approximation and complexity bounds for Bayesian KANs. We then extend to compositional Besov spaces and show that the contraction rates depend on layerwise smoothness and effective dimension of the underlying compositional structure, thereby effectively avoiding the curse of dimensionality. Together, these results advance the theoretical understanding of Bayesian neural networks and establish rigorous Bayesian guarantees for KANs.
